land.text: the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro less Montenegro, which declared independence on 3 June 2006; Serbia's parliament 'did the same' on 5 June 2006, 'effectively dissolving the union'

predecessors.note: Kosovo had been under UN administration since June 1999 and is not in Cliopatria's Serbia shape (see kosovo).

keyframe_review.note: 76,541 km2 against the infobox 77,589 km2 excluding Kosovo (ratio 0.99); the infobox total is 88,499 km2 including the disputed territory of Kosovo (ratio 0.86), so Cliopatria draws Serbia without Kosovo, as the Kosovo row (kosovo_2006) draws Kosovo. Serbia 'continues to regard Kosovo as its province', so the line between the two is disputed, not fought over; the shape is the State Union's Serbian half after Montenegro left (serbia-montenegro_2000 less montenegro_2006). Vojvodina is inside (the constitution recognises Vojvodina and Kosovo as autonomous provinces).
Same outline as 2006-2023 (76,541 km2). The article, which names Aleksandar Vučić as current president after the 2017 and 2022 elections, reports no border change after 2006.

region.text: Serbia without Kosovo: the State Union's Serbian half

ledger.note: 5 June 2006: Serbia declares independence two days after Montenegro, and the State Union ends. 'Montenegro's parliament formally declared independence on 3 June 2006'; 'Subsequently, on 5 June 2006, Serbia's parliament did the same, effectively dissolving the union' (referendum of 21 May 2006, 55.5 percent for). The Serbia page: the union 'was dissolved in 2006'; infobox 'Republic of Serbia, 2006'. The page names Serbia, not its limits; leaving Kosovo out is the researcher's reading (UN-administered since 1999, Cliopatria's Kosovo row).

certainty.note: Serbia's outer line is an international frontier on every side except Kosovo (the pages opened give no demarcation dates). The line with Kosovo is the former provincial boundary: Kosovo declared independence on 17 February 2008 and Serbia, which 'opposed the move, considering it illegal and illegitimate', continues to regard Kosovo as its province, so that line is sharp on the map but disputed in status.

notes: Written by eu-22-h on 2026-11-01 from two pages (budget 1-2). Same state or not: Cliopatria has this 2006-2024 row under Wikidata Q403 beside the older 'Serbs', 'Kingdom of Serbia' and 'Serbia' rows; the infobox lists Principality 1815, Kingdom 1882, Yugoslavia 1918, constituent republic 1945, 'Serbia and Montenegro, 1992' and 'Republic of Serbia, 2006' as formation dates. This dossier follows Cliopatria and the serbia-montenegro dossier, which names republic-of-serbia as its successor; whether the colour agent gives it the older Serbian states' colour (shared family 'balkans') is theirs. Native names: Србија (Srbija) and Република Србија are the conventional forms; the fetch tool returned no Serbian-language name for the lead sentence of the article, so they are not read from the page. Dates: the Serbia page text returned no day for the 2006 dissolution or the 2008 declaration; both come from the Serbia and Montenegro page (5 June 2006) and the Kosovo page (17 February 2008, in the kosovo dossier). No wars: no armed conflict involving Serbia's border after 2006 appears on the pages opened; the 1998-1999 Kosovo War belongs to serbia-montenegro and kosovo. No rulers: the Serbia page lists no presidents (it names only Aleksandar Vučić as current), so identity.rulers is omitted. Kosovo: the dispute is not fighting, so no contest is drawn; see the kosovo dossier. Not settled: any frontier change with Croatia, Hungary, Romania or Bulgaria after 2006 (no page opened gives one). end 2024 follows Cliopatria; the state is alive.
